clue.text: Why very little candlelight in part of Ireland?

parts.note: the question is answered by the phrase 'wick low': a candle gives little light when its wick burns low
the second half of the answering phrase, describing the wick as burning low

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about why a candle gives so little light, set somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The question gets the reply 'wick low', said as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicklow is a county on the east coast of the Republic, south of Dublin.

clue.text: Punishment — why?

definitions.meaning: to give someone ... is to scold or punish them
'...?' asks the reason, the same as 'why?'

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: a severe scolding, and a plain request for the reason behind something.

clue.text: Being exposed to disrepute, made concessions

definitions.meaning: a person whose reputation is put at risk is said to be ...
to compromise is to settle by each side giving ground

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a damaged or endangered standing and the past tense of settling by mutual concessions.

clue.text: Overtakes us in error

parts.note: a leading runner laps, or overtakes, slower ones on a track

explanation.surface: Someone passes us on the road by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsus is the Latin-derived word for a slip or mistake, as in lapsus linguae.

clue.text: Not granulated salt, say, from this supplier

parts.note: something not ground into granules is whole

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a salt is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A trader who supplies coarse rather than fine salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks for the sound of SAILOR, spelt SALER. 'Salt' looks like something from the kitchen, but here it is a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler supplies goods in bulk to retailers, so is a kind of supplier.

clue.text: Heinous acts within the organisation

indicators.note: acts suggests the letters perform and so get rearranged

explanation.surface: Wicked deeds are going on inside the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acts' turns HEINOUS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In-house work is done by a firm's own staff rather than outsiders, so it stays inside the organisation.

clue.text: Smooth succinct summary of Reagan's autobiography

parts.note: an autobiographer writes about the self, I
Ron is the short form of Ronald, Reagan's first name

explanation.surface: A brief summary of the life story of the American president Ronald Reagan.
explanation.walkthrough: A short title for Reagan's own story would be 'I, Ron'; 'succinct summary of' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron cloth is to smooth out its creases.

clue.text: Form of restraint could make lad choke

indicators.note: could make says the letters can be turned into something else

explanation.surface: A wrestling hold so tight that a boy would gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges LAD CHOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlock is a wrestling hold gripping the opponent's head under the arm, restraining them.

clue.text: Fuzz oddly rejected one kind of weapon

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions are thrown out, keeping the second and fourth

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The police turned down a particular gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuzz' is slang for the police, but here it is just letters: dropping its first and third leaves UZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun.

clue.text: From dying fire snatch book about writer

indicators.note: snatch means the letter for book is grabbed out of the word

parts.note: embers are the glowing remains of a fire dying down
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone rescues a book from the embers.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing B from EMBERS leaves EMERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist and poet.

clue.text: Maybe rifle a room

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone ransacks a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a verb, to ransack, but it is the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is one example of an arm, a weapon, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Supporting the case for Latin is likely to cause annoyance

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
the vocative is a grammatical case in Latin used for addressing someone

explanation.surface: Arguing for the teaching of Latin is bound to irritate people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like an argument, but it is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something provocative is liable to provoke, stirring irritation or anger.

clue.text: Lots and lots of money

definitions.meaning: lots are destinies or fates, as in one's lot in life
a fortune is a large sum of money

explanation.definitionFit: The plural word means both people's fates and large sums of wealth.

clue.text: Look into wage reductions resulting in strikes

indicators.note: into means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: pay cuts are reductions in wages
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: An investigation of pay cuts leads to industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' suggests walkouts; it means blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouts are heavy blows, so strikes as nouns.

clue.text: Not occupied after university, half-heartedly want practice to enter

parts.note: uni is the informal short form of university

indicators.note: to enter says one word goes inside another
half of the word's central pair of letters is lost

parts.note: to want is to need
a habit is a regular practice

explanation.surface: Unemployed after graduating, someone half wants to take up a regular routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two middle letters, leaving NED; 'to enter' puts the practice inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere uninhabited has no residents, so is not occupied.

clue.text: Marrying maiden at end of morning? Be stoical about it

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written

indicators.note: about means the phrase goes round the letter

parts.note: 'chin up' urges someone to stay brave and stoical

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A young woman is to wed at the end of the morning and must keep her nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like the bride, but gives M (a cricket over with no runs scored); 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching up couples is pairing them, so marrying in the sense of joining together.

clue.text: Frost's dated poetry

definitions.meaning: an archaic spelling of rhyme, verse

explanation.definitionFit: The word means white frost on surfaces and is an old spelling for verse, as in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Judge confronting murderer in a key work of fiction

indicators.note: confronting means standing in front of, so it comes first
in means the murderer goes inside

parts.note: key and main both mean principal
Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A judge faces a killer in a crucial piece of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The murderer of Genesis is placed inside 'a key' near its end; 'confronting' puts the judge in front of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica Inn is a novel by Daphne du Maurier, set on Bodmin Moor in Cornwall.

clue.text: Most outstanding Frenchman writing about the lower classes

indicators.note: about means the writer's name goes round the classes

parts.note: Marcel Proust was a French novelist
D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification

explanation.surface: A French author writes about the working classes at his finest.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades social classes A to E; D and E are the lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: Proudest can mean most splendid or impressive, as in a proud display.

clue.text: Guard receives info about revolutionary activity

indicators.note: receives means taking the other pieces inside

parts.note: to insure is to protect or guard against loss
gen is British slang for information
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A security guard is given intelligence about a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard' looks like a person but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgence is an uprising, so revolutionary activity against authority.

clue.text: Thick coat required, and top, as I'm shivering

indicators.note: shivering shakes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: I'm shivering, so I need a thick coat and a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' rearranges TOP AS I'M; 'coat' is a layer of paint, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint laid on thickly so brushstrokes stand out: a thick coat.

clue.text: Criminal kept huge stashes

indicators.note: stashes means the words hide the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A crook kept huge hoards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stashes' looks like a noun, but it is the verb hiding the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent criminal.

clue.text: Author reaches end of career more concerned about the environment

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A writer finishing his career turns greener.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means environmentally minded, so greener is more so.

clue.text: One wallops child held by sister

indicators.note: held by puts one piece within the other

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A sister holds a little child who hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiter is someone who smites, strikes hard: one who wallops.

clue.text: From the outset passengers hate being stuck on platform

indicators.note: from the outset takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: odium is general hatred

explanation.surface: Passengers dislike being stranded on a railway platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised platform for a speaker or winner.

clue.text: Story about the Italian Mafia leader likely to get shot?

indicators.note: about means the story goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a fable is a story
il is Italian for the

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tale about a Mafia boss who might end up gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire, but means filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something filmable is suitable for being shot with a camera.

clue.text: Topless chap in party wants kiss, the horny beast

indicators.note: topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: Tory is the Conservative Party in Britain
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A shirtless man at a party wants a kiss, the randy beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chap in' is the surface's link; 'horny' means having horns, not lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is an African antelope with long straight horns.

clue.text: Coach has struggle to contain actor's latest attack of nerves

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach

indicators.note: to contain means the fight surrounds the letter

parts.note: a fight is a struggle

indicators.note: latest takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drama coach must cope with an actor's latest bout of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a trainer but is the horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage fright is nervousness before performing, an attack of nerves.

clue.text: Expert runner knows no limits

indicators.note: no limits means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a racer is a runner

explanation.surface: A skilled runner is boundlessly able.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is a highly skilled person, an expert.

clue.text: Barrel holding many gallons — a large number, you say

indicators.note: you say signals a word spoken aloud

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: A cask containing a vast quantity, so they claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask for wine or beer.

clue.text: Hanging from cab, end drops off exhaust

parts.note: something hanging over is suspended above

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a taxi is a cab

explanation.surface: Something hanging from a taxi falls off the end of the exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like a car part but is a verb meaning tire out.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtax is to make excessive demands, wearing someone out.

clue.text: RADA pro making unexpected appearance in Grand Hotel

indicators.note: the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A drama-school professional makes a surprise appearance in a grand hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art; 'in Grand' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A parador is a state-run hotel in Spain, often a historic building.
